questions.question: What is the purpose of a scientific report's abstract?
choices: List every raw data value
Replace the complete methods section
Summarize the question, approach, main findings, and conclusion
Present only the author's biography

questions.question: Which section usually explains how data were collected?
choices: References
Methods
Title
Acknowledgments

questions.question: Which section primarily presents observations and measurements?
choices: Discussion
References
Acknowledgments
Results

questions.question: Which section commonly interprets findings and their limitations?
choices: Discussion
Abstract only
Methods only
Results without interpretation

questions.question: What is the purpose of citing a source?
choices: Credit prior work and help readers locate supporting information
Guarantee the cited claim is correct
Replace all original evidence
Hide the origin of an idea

questions.question: What is a figure caption?
choices: A list of all authors' qualifications
A replacement for the graph's data
Text explaining a figure's content, symbols, and relevant conditions
A statement that figures need no units

questions.question: What is plagiarism?
choices: Reporting results that challenge an earlier explanation
Using another person's work or ideas without appropriate acknowledgment
Repeating a published procedure while crediting its source
Using a standard term such as mass or velocity

questions.question: Why should methods describe sampling and measurement procedures?
choices: Methods should guarantee that all conclusions are correct
Readers do not need to understand comparisons
Procedures are relevant only if results agree
Readers need to evaluate how the evidence was obtained

questions.question: Why should scientific reports distinguish results from interpretations?
choices: Only interpretations can be numerical
Measurements and explanations play different roles in assessing a claim
Results are always personal opinions
Both sections must contain identical sentences

questions.question: Why are units and labeled axes necessary in a scientific figure?
choices: They help readers interpret the represented quantities
They make the sample automatically unbiased
They guarantee a causal relationship
They replace the need to describe data collection

questions.question: Why does peer review not guarantee that a paper contains no errors?
choices: Reviewers never examine methods
Published data cannot be questioned
Review can identify issues but is limited by available evidence and scrutiny
Every paper is tested under every possible condition

questions.question: Why is sharing appropriate data and analysis details useful?
choices: It guarantees every reanalysis reaches the same result
It eliminates all privacy and consent obligations
It makes interpretation unnecessary
It allows others to inspect and build on the findings

questions.question: Why should limitations be included in a report?
choices: They clarify the conditions and strength of the conclusions
They prove the entire study has no value
They belong only in unpublished work
They permit researchers to invent missing data

questions.question: Why must a paraphrase still acknowledge its source?
choices: Only exact quotations need credit
Paraphrases automatically become experimental data
Citations are needed only for images
Changing wording does not remove the origin of the borrowed idea

questions.question: How should a correction to a published result be communicated?
choices: Replace data silently without explanation
Clearly identify the change and its effect on the conclusions
Delete all mention of the original methods
Report only that the title changed

questions.question: A graph shows temperature but its vertical axis is labeled only 'Value.' What improves communication?
choices: Remove the numerical scale without adding units
Replace measured values with unlabeled category names
Add the quantity and temperature unit
Use only an author's name as the axis label

questions.question: A report says an experiment was repeated but gives no trial count. What information should be added?
choices: Only the highest recorded result
Only the overall average without the trial count
Only the word repeated without numerical details
The number of trials and relevant procedure details

questions.question: A reviewer identifies a possible uncontrolled variable. What is a constructive response?
choices: Reject the concern because a reviewer disagreed
Hide the relevant methods
Evaluate the concern and clarify, limit, or revise the study as needed
Assume peer review makes new testing unnecessary

questions.question: A presentation claims a result applies to all students, but only one class was studied. What wording is more defensible?
choices: Describe the studied class and state limits on generalization
Keep the universal claim without qualification
Claim that every school was sampled
Omit how participants were selected

questions.question: A student uses another researcher's graph in a presentation. What is appropriate?
choices: Remove the author's name and claim original measurements
Provide attribution and follow any applicable permission or license requirements
Change the colors so attribution is unnecessary
Treat every online graph as unrestricted original work
